name: Supercreator
subcategory: creator DM automation and agency tooling
tagline: AI chat replies, mass messaging, scheduling and analytics layered on top of subscription creator platforms like OnlyFans.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The part people actually feel every day, an AI that reads the thread and drafts three replies in the creator's voice, is a browser extension plus one LLM call. An agent can produce that in a sitting, and it will work for a solo creator running one account. What it will not produce is the durable half: scheduled mass DMs that do not trip rate limits, PPV tracking, multi-chatter team dashboards, shift handoffs, and a vendor whose whole job is patching the integration every time the host platform changes its DOM or tightens automation rules. That last point is the real cost, since the platform has no public API and automation lives in a grey zone that can cost you the account. Build it if you are one person who wants better drafts, not if you are running an agency.
coreLoopDIY: A local Chrome extension that reads the open chat thread, sends it to an LLM with your persona and pricing notes, and offers three insertable reply drafts plus saved snippets.
requirements: Chrome or another Chromium browser you control
An OpenAI or Anthropic API key in .env or extension options
A written persona file: voice, boundaries, price list, standard upsells
Acceptance that DOM scraping breaks on every platform redesign
Your own read on the host platform's rules about automation
whatYouLose: Mass messaging and scheduled sends with sane throttling, the feature that actually moves revenue
Agency layer: multiple chatters, seats, shift handoff, per-chatter performance
Vault and PPV management, media libraries, price testing and conversion tracking
Someone else maintaining the integration when the host platform changes its markup or clamps down
Analytics across accounts and any historical baseline to compare yourself against
moatNotes: The integration is unofficial by necessity, which is exactly why paying someone to maintain it has value: their breakage is their problem, not your Saturday.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the money in this niche is in volume and coordination, not in one clever reply. Agencies pay for seats, shift tracking, mass send scheduling and PPV analytics across many accounts, and for a vendor who ships a patch within hours when the host platform quietly changes something. A solo creator with a homemade drafting extension gets maybe sixty percent of the daily comfort and zero percent of the operational scaffolding, and the moment the extension breaks mid shift they are the on call engineer.
notes: The reply drafter is a weekend build; the mass send engine and the agency console are not.
prompt:
Build a local-only Chrome extension (Manifest V3, plain TypeScript, Vite, no framework) called "Draftbox" that helps one person write DM replies faster on a subscription creator platform. It is a personal tool: no backend, no accounts, no telemetry, no analytics.

Stack, non negotiable:
- Vite + TypeScript, output an unpacked MV3 extension in dist/
- Side panel UI (chrome.sidePanel), vanilla DOM, one CSS file, no component library
- chrome.storage.local for persona, snippets and settings
- Direct fetch to the Anthropic Messages API from the side panel; key stored in chrome.storage.local via an options page, never hardcoded, and document that a .env is only used for local dev scripts

Core loop:
1. A content script scrapes the currently open chat thread from the page using CSS selectors defined in one editable file, selectors.ts, with a comment block at the top saying "these WILL break, edit here"
2. It sends the last 20 messages plus who sent what to the side panel
3. The side panel calls the model with: the thread, a persona.md style text field the user edits (voice, boundaries, price list, standard upsells), and asks for exactly 3 candidate replies with different intents: warm, upsell, deflect
4. Each candidate has a Copy button and an Insert button; Insert asks the content script to type the text into the composer element and focus it, without sending
5. A snippets tab: named reusable lines, click to insert, editable, stored locally
6. A tone slider with three fixed values (short, normal, chatty) that changes only the prompt

Explicitly out of scope, do not build: mass or bulk sending, scheduling, auto send without a human click, multi account switching, PPV or payment tracking, team seats, any server, any database, any cloud sync.

Safety and honesty requirements:
- Never auto submit a message. Insert only.
- On first run show a one screen notice that scraping and automating a third party site may violate its terms and can get an account banned, with an "I understand" button
- No network calls except the model API. Assert this in the README.

Deliverables: working dist/ build, README with load-unpacked steps, selectors.ts with placeholder selectors and instructions for finding real ones via devtools, and a persona.example.md. Keep the whole thing under about 800 lines.
